group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed counts measured for Aqeilan RI on 2026-08-10 and retained in the PMID42422765 manifest; local 2026-08-14 Aqeilan audit found 66 matching WWOX-corpus records.
group_assessment.weighting: Foundational WWOX experimental laboratory, but not a primary WWOX developmental-epileptic-encephalopathy group in this 2013 oncology study. The interaction observations receive primary-mechanism weight; disease translation remains weak.
group_assessment.note: The team has direct WWOX and p63 expertise; that strengthens assay provenance but does not repair the transformed-cell and overexpression limits.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where does LEGEND attribute ITCH/proteasomal stabilization to PMID 23370280, and is the stabilized object WWOX or ΔNp63α?
corpus_crossquery.finding: The load-bearing error is bullet 3 of CC-20260810-41984841-01. Salah 2013 stabilizes ΔNp63α by WWOX-mediated competition against ITCH; ITCH/K63-associated stabilization of WWOX belongs to PMID 24550385. A superseding commit candidate and DL-MECH-104 preserve the correction append-only.

retraction_check.result: No retraction, expression of concern or correction for PMID 23370280.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Structured PMC XML and nine-page PDF are local and fingerprinted. All six native figures and all 23 labelled panels were visually inspected; the article declares no tables or supplementary material.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: Every textual locator is drawn from Results, Discussion or Methods rather than the abstract; visual locators point to fingerprinted native JPEGs.

entries.proposition: WWOX binds ΔNp63α through WW1 in these co-immunoprecipitation/pulldown systems.
entries.snippet: While a physical interaction was revealed between WWOX and ΔNp63α, WWOX-Y33R abolished this interaction

entries.proposition: The canonical ΔNp63α PPxY motif is not required for the observed WWOX association.
entries.snippet: Unexpectedly, ΔNp63α-AAxA was still able to bind WWOX similar to intact ΔNp63α

entries.proposition: WWOX antagonizes ITCH-driven ubiquitination of ΔNp63α.
entries.snippet: We found that while expression of ITCH increases ubiquitination of ΔNp63α (Figure 3a, middle lane), coexpression of WWOX abrogated this ubiquitination event
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination and degradation mediated by ITCH

entries.proposition: WWOX competes with ITCH for ΔNp63α and this depends on the WWOX interaction surface.
entries.snippet: We found that while WWOX expression reduced the interaction between ΔNp63α and ITCH, WWOX-Y33R was unable to do so
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination and degradation mediated by ITCH

entries.proposition: The stabilized object in the cycloheximide experiment is ΔNp63α, not WWOX.
entries.snippet: Whereas WWOX led to increased half-life of ΔNp63α, WWOX-Y33R mutant that does not interact with ΔNp63α (Figure 2), had little effect if at all, on ΔNp63α half-life
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination and degradation mediated by ITCH

entries.proposition: Endogenous WWOX depletion is associated with lower ΔNp63α abundance in HaCaT cells.
entries.snippet: WWOX-depleted HaCaT (KD) cells displayed lower ΔNp63α levels compared with control shRNA-expressing (EV) cells
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination and degradation mediated by ITCH

entries.proposition: WWOX shifts ΔNp63α from nuclear toward cytoplasmic localization.
entries.snippet: although ΔNp63α alone localizes mainly in the nuclear fraction, coexpression of ΔNp63α and WWOX was associated with increased ΔNp63α presence in the cytoplasm concomitant with less nuclear ΔNp63α levels
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX sequesters ΔNp63α in the cytoplasm

entries.proposition: WWOX suppresses ΔNp63α transcriptional output despite increasing its abundance.
entries.snippet: coexpression of WWOX with ΔNp63α significantly suppressed ΔNp63α transactivation function in a dose-dependent manner
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX suppresses ΔNp63α transactivation ability

entries.proposition: Doxycycline independently causes cell death in the assay system and therefore confounds Figure 6 interpretation.
entries.snippet: We observed that treatment of Dox alone induces cell death by 2.6-fold as compared with untreated cells

entries.proposition: All study cell lines lack normal p53 function, limiting generalization.
entries.snippet: In all cell lines used in this article, p53 function is lost by different mechanisms, including mutation and loss of expression and function
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, Cell culture and transient transfection

entries.proposition: Figure 1 supports selective WWOX association with ΔNp63α but also exposes a failed initial reverse co-IP.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1 panels a-d show ΔNp63α-associated WWOX signal across co-IP and GST-pulldown configurations; the lower reverse co-IP in panel a lacks the specific signal that motivated panel d.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 visually supports WW1 dependence and noncanonical binding despite the ΔNp63α AAxA mutation.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2 panels a-c: Y33R loses the ΔNp63α pulldown, WW1-containing constructs carry the interaction, and ΔNp63α-AAxA retains visible WWOX association without quantitative densitometry.
entries.qualifies_needle: still able to bind WWOX similar to intact ΔNp63α

entries.proposition: Figure 3 establishes the correct substrate and direction but relies mainly on overexpression blots with limited quantification.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3 panels a-f: WWOX reduces ITCH-mediated ΔNp63α ubiquitination/association and lengthens ΔNp63α stability; the panels do not show ITCH stabilizing WWOX and most lack densitometry or inferential statistics.

entries.proposition: Figure 4 supports partial cytoplasmic redistribution rather than complete sequestration.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4 panels a-c show increased cytoplasmic ΔNp63α with WWOX, while nuclear ΔNp63α remains visible in a subset and the authors leave other localization regulators possible.
entries.qualifies_needle: increased ΔNp63α presence in the cytoplasm

entries.proposition: Figure 5 supports transcriptional suppression but Y33R only partially attenuates it and statistical details are sparse.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5 panels a-c show dose-dependent reporter suppression by WWOX and residual suppression with Y33R; error bars are shown but the plotted panels do not identify the inferential test or significance marks.

entries.proposition: Figure 6 does not isolate WWOX-specific chemosensitization because doxycycline itself changes cell death.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6 panels a-d show cisplatin-associated death alongside a control in which doxycycline alone raises death and further increases the cisplatin response; this prevents clean attribution to induced ΔNp63α/WWOX alone.
entries.qualifies_needle: Dox alone induces cell death by 2.6-fold
